newsitem.title: UK: Smiths' Hurn to stay put after succession.
newsitem.headline: Smiths' Hurn to stay put after succession.

text.p: Smiths Industries Plc's chairman and chief executive Sir Roger Hurn said on Wednesday that the chairmanship would remain his main business interest after he gives up his role as chief executive in November.

Newly-appointed director Keith Butler-Wheelhouse is due take over as chief executive on November 19, leaving Hurn as chairman. "We are going to work very closely together and I am looking forward to it," Hurn told a results news conference.
Hurn said he should be regarded neither as an executive or non-executive chairman in future, but simply as the chairman.
"I am not applying any adjectives to it (my title)...But he (Butler-Wheelhouse) is going to be boss."
Hurn has been chief executive for 12 years and joint chairman and chief executive for the last five.

The company has gradually weaned itself off dependence on the aerospace industry as its biggest single business, spending over 475 million stg from cashflow since 1990 on acquisitions for its medical and industrial divisions.
Annual pretax profits have grown from 103.4 million stg in 1991/92 to 165.4 million stg on sales up 54 percent to 1.008 billion stg in the year just ended.
Butler-Wheelhouse, who joined the company as a director in August, said his main task in his first year as chief executive will be to maintain the momentum for growth.
"It's nice to come into a business that doesn't need a lot of things doing to it," said the former chief exectutive of Sweden's Saab Automobile.
"I am very impressed by the quality of the management and the "no frills no nonsense approach...strong internal controls and highly motivated people," he said.
